lines: The platform of Kita-Senju Station
The silver ticket gates
Trading old stories, deep in longing
On the bench where we sat down
We can't see a thing
But we swore ourselves to the future
The trees and the cat, enduring the cold
As if it were all about us
Shake themselves, trying to bring their buds into bloom
Smiling beautifully
There's no need to rush
Someday, become a bouquet for me
Until then, please wait
Whatever unfolds from here, the two of us
Will live through it until we tire of it
While conveying the bare minimum of love
I wonder what kind of future
Is peering this way at us
If we share your strength and my weakness
What amazing things might happen?
Look, we're already this happy
Someday, one
Someday, two
Let's keep adding to what matters
Drifting through Kita-Senju Station
An indigo skirt
Looks farther away than it ever has, so far, so far
Footsteps accelerating
I felt like I had to
Stop being so stubborn
Leaning too much on your kindness
For the back of a man too frightened
To rest a hand on him gently — that could only be
You, walking ahead of me
Please, let the future
Wave its hand toward us
The hardship of each day and my body
Keep searching shamelessly for a place to come home to
Look, the sunset is already this deep
When I recall the lights of that day
I suppose I'll come to notice what matters
There's no need to rush
Someday, become a bouquet for me
We can't see a thing
But we swore ourselves to the future
I wonder what kind of future
Is peering this way at us
If we share your strength and my weakness
What amazing things might happen?
Look, we're already this happy
Someday, one
Someday, two
No — more, and more still
Let's keep adding to what matters
The platform of the station we've long called home
Greeting the pale blue
"Welcome home," it says
The happiness of stepping on a small, swaying shadow
